item.title: [Segurança] Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
item.description:
🚨 Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
 
Criticidade: Alta
Ferramenta: Qualys
Fonte: The Hacker News
CVSS: N/D
Resumo:
Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open. The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.
Link: https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/critical-flaw-in-pythons-popular-pillow.html

item.title: [Segurança] Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
item.description:
🚨 Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
 
Criticidade: Média
Ferramenta: Qualys
Fonte: The Hacker News
CVSS: 4.2
Resumo:
Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated. Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or custom build, by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497).
Link: https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/researchers-demonstrate-node2shell-rce.html
